utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because mortars are also weapons that have great firepower.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If we are talking about artillery and mortars are not artillery pieces, why are you dealing with this at all? Why are you dealing with the characteristics of the artillery as a combat arm of the army? Were you asked to deal with artillery as a combat arm of the army?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically as a combat arm of the army. That is why I said artillery and mortars in my heading. Yes, that's what I said, artillery and mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And this sentence where it says: "The artillery is a combat arm of the army that has great firepower," what does this sentence have to do with an infantry battalion or a motorised battalion from the infantry combat arm? It is my assertion that it has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, specifically it does not have anything to do with it, but it has to do with the definition in terms of what artillery is as a notion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So what you say here has to do with artillery as a combat arm, not the infantry or specifically an infantry battalion or a motorised battalion?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the combat arm of the artillery, but I would like to mention once again that I am referring to 120-millimetre mortars as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you look at the next page -- just a moment, Your Honour, please. Page 8, please, in B/C/S -- or actually page 7, Mr. Poje. That is question number 9, where you say: "The difference between artillery and mortars," that's what you say under subheading (a). Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the following page, that is page number 8, you define mortars; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please -- sorry, just a moment. Mr. Poje, when you define the characteristics of a mortar on the one hand, and the artillery on the other hand, you say: "Cannons are artillery weapons..." Howitzers are artillery weapons..." Howitzer guns are artillery weapons. As far as mortars are concerned, quite rightly, in my opinion, you do not say that mortars are artillery weapons. So that's why I'm asking you the following: Is it correct that a mortar is an infantry weapon aimed at firing at personnel with weapons that are in open spaces and in natural or man-made shelters? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not say "infantry weapon," it just says "weapon."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking you. Is it correct that a mortar is an infantry weapon used to fire at personnel and weapons located in open spaces and natural man-made shelters?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If mortars are infantry weapons, as we already have said here, that sentence could be supplemented in this way as you have proposed, to say mortars are infantry weapons used to, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the last sentence from this segment that has to do with mortars, you say that a mortar can be fired from ravines, valleys, forests. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In principle, is a mortar a proper weapon to be used from behind cover?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of characteristics of mortars that use an upper angle, that is to say that they are fired from behind cover, even bigger shelters like a big forest, even a forest, if it has certain clearings, that makes it possible to carry out transfers. So in principle, mortars are used from a covered firing position against targets that are perhaps concealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So as you said, it can be used from a forest that, say, has a small clearing?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have to be a biggish clearing. I'm sorry for interrupting. It depends on how high the trees actually are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It can also be used from behind a high building, a relatively high building, four- or five-storey buildings; right

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there has to be an appropriate distance so the trajectory can go above the building, because of course it's easier to use a mortar to go above that building than to use a Howitzer cannon or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It can be used behind a high wall, too; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be used behind a wall, but it doesn't mean that it's right by the wall. It means that what has to be done is that it has to be far enough from the obstacle which we use at cover so that, given a certain range, we can actually hit the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If, for example, a building is 15 metres high, how far away does the weapon have to be from the building concerned in order to be able to fire? For example, under a -- with an elevation angle of 80 degrees or 81, 2, 3, 5 degrees?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the firing tables and in the combat rules there are instructions for this. I cannot do it off-the-cuff just now, but there is a minimum range involved so that in order to be able to go above the building or obstacle that is in front of the mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So firing tables can be used?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If the elevation angle is 45 degrees, that means that the smallest distance between the weapon and the wall would be the height of the wall itself. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If the elevation angle is bigger than 45 degrees, that means that the distance between the weapon and the wall would have to be shorter than the actual height of the wall.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the elevation goes down, as the barrel is lowered, that means that practically the trajectory is lower. That means that we have to move further away from the obstacle that is in front of the mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Poje, if the elevation is 45 degrees, that means that the weapon has to be at a distance which equals the height of the wall. If the elevation is more than 45 degrees, that means the weapon can be even closer to the wall. The distance does not have to be at least the height of the wall itself, it can be less; right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 10, of your report that is, in B/C/S. That is the section that has to do with rocket projectiles. Please be so kind as to tell us the following: In the first paragraph, you talk about rocket projectiles and then you give an example of an M63, 128-millimetre multiple rocket launcher, don't you?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This weapon has nothing to do with infantry weapons; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there's a rocket projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. Could you please explain that.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking of the definition of the rocket projectile. One type of a rocket projectile is a multi-launcher M63 128. This does not appear in the actual circumstances, it's just a definition of what a rocket projectile is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question was there you mention a multi-barrel rocket launcher, and you agree with me that a multi-rocket launcher is not an infantry weapon.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. A multiple-rocket launcher is not an infantry weapon. Again, I mentioned it because it's a rocket projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: An Osa and a Zolja are rocket projectiles in the infantry arm units?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And they're not mentioned here in this report as an example which is much more appropriate than a multiple-rocket launcher as an example of a rocket projectile.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I thought a rocket was a rocket, so whether it was one kind or another, well, I just cited one example of a rocket projectile. I just remembered a multiple-rocket launcher, and I said that this rocket was one of a possible rocket projectiles, a 120 millimetre one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: An anti-tank guided rocket 9K11 is an infantry weapon, an infantry weapon belonging to the infantry armed units.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to move to question number 10, Mr. Poje, and that is the question of direct and indirect fire. Could you please just keep your answers short, and I'm hoping that you will be able to confirm my suggestions. Direct firing is more precise than indirect or semi-direct fire?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When we're talking about indirect fire, the use of artillery observation points increases the expenditure of artillery ammunition?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When we have indirect fire, the probability of getting hits is reduced?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: With indirect fire, the dispersion of the projectile increases?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the positions that you saw yesterday on the map of the 2nd of December, the battalion firing group 3 at the Uskoplje position was able to execute only indirect firing in view of how far it was away from the forward part of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was only indirect firing that was possible. Had it been direct firing, the target should have been visible from the position where the weapon was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the Strincjera position -- Mr. Poje, would it be easier for you to have the map before you or are you familiar enough with the terrain?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I can go on without the map, and if I do need the map I'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please let us know. From the Strincjera position, it's possible only to execute indirect hits from [as interpreted] the anti-aircraft gun north of the Old Town or Bogisica Park or the Gradac Park or from the positions at Ploce east of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only indirect fire was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, I would just like to be -- briefly go through the part of the report that deals with the 120-millimetre light mortar. That is on page 11. Purpose and combat characteristics.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there's a mistake in the transcript. Page 50, line 12 -- or actually that question from the Strincjera position it's possible only to execute indirect hits. It says from the anti-aircraft gun north. I think it should be to the anti-aircraft gun. I think that it's important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you, my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We already reviewed the question of artillery weapons on page 11, so we will not go back to that. I'm interested -- on page 12, I'm interested in the technical and tactical data. You mention here in the beginning active-reactive shells with the motor on, active-reactive shells with the motor off. You also mention on page 13 the 120-millimetre mine AR TF M77. This is under number 1, and under number 2 you mention the 120-millimetre mine TF OF-843/1. Is it correct that both of these mines - and we are talking about two types of active-reactive mines, that they are not mentioned in any of the firing tables in the period that we're discussing, the period of 1991?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: These things that refer to active-reactive shells are not contained in the firing tables. There is no information in the firing tables about those mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information that those mines were used in 1991 in the sector that we are discussing here, October, November, December 1991, in and around Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the report drafted by the UNESCO commission and together with the commission of the government of the Republic of Croatia, I found one, two, or three examples, I cannot tell you exactly how many, stating that it was possible that active-reactive shells were used. To tell you the truth, the last firing with mortars in the JNA that I executed was in 1991. Throughout the whole time that I was in the artillery training centre, we never fired. We mentioned that shell. We know that such shells exist, but we never actually fired such shells. So I did not actually ever see this type of shell myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you saw that in a report as a possibility that they were used. Could you please kindly just focus on my question.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the report that I mentioned, on several occasions, maybe two or three times, it was mentioned that amongst 2.000 hits, I found it written that an active-reactive shell was used. I didn't see that myself and I'm not saying myself that these mines -- shells were actually fired. I'm just confirming or repeating what is stated in that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Knowing the fact that in 1991 there were no firing tables for those two shells in the JNA, and in view of your experience that throughout all of your years of experience you never fired such shells, do you agree with me the possibility that JNA units had such shells is very slight?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the probability is very slight, almost non-existent that units, that units JNA -- that the JNA units had at their disposal these active-reactive shells, especially since the basic fire tables that were used in order to determine the 120-millimetre mortar elements and M75 mortar elements do not contain information about those shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On page 15, please, would you look at your clarification of anti-aircraft guided rockets 9K11, and could you just please tell us whether this weapon, besides opening fire on tank or armoured targets, can be successfully used against bunkers, fortified -- and fortified buildings?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Tanks, APCs, bunkers, fortified buildings, and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Page 16 of the B/C/S version, under (b), distribution of fire. Can you see that, sir? For the 120-millimetre mortar, you define the effective zone of projectiles -- the width of the effective zone of projectiles, on average, as 60 metres.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please kindly tell us, where did you find this data in the firing tables?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it in the artillery rules of firing, in the section that deals with the use and the quantity of ammunition that needs to be used, the ammunition expenditure. One column speaks about the effective zone of the projectiles themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, that is not the effective zone. This is something quite different. So I'm asking you, please, to look at the firing tables for the MB 120, and can you show us there from the firing tables. If we have the same edition, perhaps you can turn to page 20 and show us the effective zone of projectiles for that weapon. Does it not state there that it is 70 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the semi-axis is 70 metres, so the axis would be 34 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If the firing table gives as the axis of the effective zone as 34 metres, why does it say in your report 60 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the data about the effective zone of projectiles of a mortar was something that I took from the normative or from the average ammunition expenditure from the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you are right. There is a mistake in the transcript. That is line 23 -- page 23, line 20. It should say 60 metres and not 70 as it states in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Poje. Let's move ahead. Page 17 of the B/C/S version. Do you see this table that is given here?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You took this table from Zivanov's Theory of Gunnery, published in 1979.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you also attached that. You mention that in a footnote to your report.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you have the report in B/C/S or in Serbo-Croatian? Do you have that page in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. If you have that page in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, Your Honour. I would like to find this page also for you, so please, if you could bear with me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we are still confused by the answers at around 53, 19 and following. 70 metres is given as the effective zone and the semi-axis; and then at 22, the firing table gives the axis zone of 34 metres. Why does it say in your report 60? And then at page 54, line 4, you put the question whether it should be 60 metres and not 70. I'm afraid we haven't been able to follow all of that. It would make sense if you meant 17 metres rather than 70 metres, the reference to 34 metres. I'm using separate numerals to try and avoid the confusion between 17 and 70 in speech, but there may be some other sense of this. We haven't grasped it yet, and I mention it in case you can clarify it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will clarify that right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, in your report, on page -- on page 16, it states that the width or the radius of the average effective zone of projectiles is 60 metres.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: For a 120-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Then I asked you to look at the firing tables for the 120-millimetre mortar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the firing tables, the 120-millimetre mortar is supposed to have a semi-axis of the effective zone of projectiles as 17 metres or an average of 34 metres.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can now follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, now we're moving to page 17 of your report, which contains a table which presents errors in the preparation of elements for group fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, in the first row, correction directly on the target gives the values of the average error Vd -- Ex (Vd) 1 by distance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And Ey (Vp) by direction, and that is 1.6; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you, in quoting this data, you say in footnote 8 of your report that you took this information from Zivanov's Gunnery Theory published in 1979; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you please look at table 62 on page 427 of the Gunnery Theory by Zivojin Zivanov. Could you please look at that table which you attached as a footnote, which is in this thick pile here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, since it is very difficult to go through it, it's not very easy to find this particular table. It is there somewhere. I saw it yesterday in the B/C/S version, but I'm not sure how I'm going to find it because everything is absolutely unmarked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please try to find -- here it is. Yes, I've found it. It's -- it looks like this. This is the cover page. We have no other markings, so I don't know how I can assist Your Honours. The cover page of the document says "Theory of firing, table 1." There is a dark page. The ERN number and the page that I am citing is 03552520, and it seems to me that the best thing to do, Your Honours, if you agree, is to place this page on the ELMO and then I can put my questions to the witness, because it's not possible for all of us to have the document in front of us. Mr. Poje, could you please look at this page. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why did you, Mr. Poje, include the data of average error and correction directly on the target elongation 1 and axis 1.6, when in the table that you quoted and that you referred to and that you attached to your expert report the average error and correction directly on the target ranges between 0.5 for Vd and 2.2, and for Vp along the axis between 0.0 and 9.0? You have different values, 1 and 1.6, which are totally different from the ones that eventually can drastically change the computation of the error. The average error, distance and axis errors given in Zivanov's table are correct, and they refer to all types of corrections and means used.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that in the table that I made in which the average error of preparation of elements for group targeting, the correction for (Vp) Ey is 1.6, refers to the correction of the measured deviations by using a laser range metre and the assessment of the hits when the last is 100 metres. If you use sonar reconnaissance units, then the average error of preparation of elements is much higher. In this particular case and in the example that I quoted, these means for sonar reconnaissance or radar units are not mentioned at all and for that reason I didn't give all the data pertaining to the range of error of preparation of elements for group firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why did you choose the average error of 1? Where did you find this figure? That's question number 1. Question number 2: Why if you have taken a copy from Zivanov's book, as you have stated in the footnote, why did you not copy it with all the elements that it included? Why did you make a selection of what you saw fit and disregarded all other data from the table that was not suitable in your mind?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only missing element is the explanation to the table that those elements refer to the correction according to the measurements made by laser range finder.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why did you not include this in your report? Why did you not include this explanation that because you thought that was the situation that you just described for us, why did you not include this in your report?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you honestly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your job, as it is the case in our job, is it permissible to quote a source and then rewrite the original version?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not without a proper explanation. I would like to reiterate that what is missing is an explanation why I put these figures instead of using the figures from the original table.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why did you not provide this explanation?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you quite frankly I don't know why I didn't do that. Perhaps I thought that it was self-explanatory and that if somebody asked me, I would be able to explain orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you chose values corresponding to average error when using a laser range finder. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the correction of the assessment of the target if the last fork is 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you find the information that a laser range finder was used for 82-millimetre and 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, one of the instruments used for these mortars, 80 and 120 millimetres, is a laser range finder too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you say that an infantry unit or a motorised unit of infantry have laser range finders and that they are being used at the level of a battalion?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they are being used. If they are not used with a bi-pod or a tripod, they are using it as kind of hand-held laser range finders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where is that written?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking from my own experience, because throughout the whole period that the units serving our school centre, the command platoon had, among other things, an artillery console, an artillery laser range finder and other instruments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You are talking about artillery. I'm asking you about infantry, an infantry or a motorised battalion. Do you understand what I'm asking you? I have no doubts that in your artillery school centre you had the equipment that you had just mentioned. My question is: How did you come about to find that an infantry unit or a motorised battalion have as one of their own instruments a laser range finder?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat again: The units that served us came from regular units. They were not part of the school centre. A mortar unit came from Kranj to serve the artillery school centre in 1990 and 1991, and they had a laser range finder.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is an RAP?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an auxiliary kit, tool kit. That means that it has certain devices in it that are used as auxiliary tools, and one of those tools is a shovel, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Among those instruments is a label -- a level, a quadrant, and surveyor poles and other things that are used in firing and without which the firing is not possible?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Also in this huge pile of documents, you gave us the contents of RAP, referring to 120 millimetres, including a level, quadrants, and surveyor's poles. However, nowhere in your documents there's a mention of a laser range finder being in the kit, referring to 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reconnaissance instruments are not part of the RAP. They are part of the command platoon. These are the instruments and means used by the command platoon and they are not part of the mortar RAP.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where is the command platoon in an infantry battalion?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In an infantry battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, mortar battery has a command platoon. Now, tell me, why -- how the command platoon that you say that exists within a mortar battery, can you first tell me where it is located?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is on observation post on the firing position, and the reconnaissance and communications officers are both on the observation posts and the firing positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What knowledge do you have about the use of laser range finder in the period October, November, December by infantry units or, rather, Motorised Battalion in and around Dubrovnik? Do you have any knowledge about that at all?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume that mortar units, 120-millimetre units, once they were shifted from infantry to -- from artillery to infantry, that everything went with them, including the weapons and all other instruments and tools for reconnaissance and other purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about October, November, December 1991. Everything that you just told us about the laser range finder was just your sheer guesswork; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am convinced that they did have laser range finders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, do you know that for a fact or is it just your assumption?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my assumption after all, for the reasons that I just told you, that once mortars were shifted to infantry, probably all the other -- all the kits and tools went with them, because while they were with artillery, they did have laser range finders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very good. That means that on page 17, where you explain in the table the errors of preparatory elements for firing, correction directly on the target, and I have full respect for what you wrote here, was based on your assumptions.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my calculations. I did at least some 20 calculations or preparatory elements for group firing, and I spent more than 13 years, and I dealt with about 40 cases like this. So if the ultimate fork of firing at a target is 100 metres, and if this is used for the correction, and if a laser range finder is used, the error is 1 Vd distance error and 1.6 Vp error.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But based on the presumption that a laser range finder was used.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the laser finder was not used, and if the correction of the hit was made, then the correction is nearly equal -- the error is nearly equal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please try to answer my question. Based on the assumption that a laser range finder was used, these values are as they are in the table?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On page 19 of your report - that's the table of expenditure of ammunition for a 120-millimetre mortar - can you tell us, please, does this table indicate, under columns B, C, D, E, F in the upper part, referring to unobserved targets, does this table mean that for neutralising only 25 per cent of the target it is necessary to spend the quoted quantities of ammunition listed under the last column to the right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This is referring to an unobserved target, and that means that is a target that cannot be seen from the mortar firing position?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it also cannot be seen from the observation point. That is why it is called an unobserved target.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. For any higher degree of neutralisation of a target, a proportionate increase of ammunition expenditure is to be expected.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you want to achieve 90 per cent, you have to triple the quantity of the ammunition used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So, for example, to neutralise 50 per cent - this is the example under C - of a platoon of mortars under cover, it is necessary to have 720 shells; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: For a higher degree of neutralisation, higher than 50 per cent, then?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: For 80 per cent neutralisation, then it has to be increased nine times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So to neutralise -- to neutralise a platoon of mortars under cover by 80 per cent, it is necessary to have 2.160 shells?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is your calculation, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I multiplied 240 by 9.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I would like to suggest to take a break now if you think the time is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I assume it would be convenient, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, before we move on to the next subject, could you please clarify something for us. Is it correct that according to establishment, infantry units of the JNA, and I primarily refer to infantry rules and all other relevant indicators, is an 82-millimetre mortar a company mortar?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that a 120-millimetre mortar is a battalion mortar?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P132, which is in tab 30 of the Jokic binder. So it's the Jokic binder, tab 30. The exhibit number is P132. Yesterday my learned friend, Mr. Weiner, showed the same map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, could you please fold the map so that we can see the town of Dubrovnik and the position of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade. Have you got that section of the map?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please place it on the ELMO, that particular section, so that everybody could follow. Mr. Poje, just briefly, since of course you are familiar with these maps, can we clarify some elements of the combat deployment of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade. First of all, I would like to ask you whether you can indicate this with a pointer on the ELMO. Could you please use the pointer to indicate what we need. First of all, from the island of Lokrum, north-east you can see a small flag where it says "3," and an ellipsis can be seen there.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's it. Tell us, please, Mr. Poje, is that the position of the anti-tank company of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This little flag, does it depict the command post?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So the forward command post. From the point of view of establishment, as you said to us yesterday, within the establishment in 1991 in the JNA, within this company of this battalion, is there a recoilless 82-millimetre gun there?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: A 911 Maljutka?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's as far as the anti-tank company is concerned and its position?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please just answer so that we have an audible answer. Now, if we look at the north-west in the region of the village of Bosanka. The 1st Motorised Company of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Further on north-east, the 2nd Company of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And north-west, at the end of this area that you're indicating on the ELMO, the 3rd Motorised Company of the 3rd Battalion. Thank you. So now could you please indicate Uskoplje for us.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And the battalion fire support group of the 3rd Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm indicating it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So let us summarise what you've said to us now. If we look at the last battalion fire support group 3 in Uskoplje and these front end positions of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd Motorised Companies, the distance is between 4.000 to 5.000 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So the distance is about 4, 4.5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. From the point of view of establishment, the Infantry Company or, rather, Motorised Infantry Company, has 82-millimetre mortars; is that right, according to establishment? Mr. Poje, could you please speak up, because otherwise we will not have your answers in the transcript. I saw you answer but we haven't got it recorded.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So within a motorised company there are 82-millimetre mortars, right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That pertains to the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Motorised Companies respectively?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The battalion fire support group has within it, as we already mentioned, battalion mortars or, rather, 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the map again if it's not a problem. In the western area, that is Petrovo Selo, that is to the north of Rijeka Dubrovacka, can you see that area? That's where the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade is. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see in the area of Pobrezje the position of an 82-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Further to the north, in the area of Greblje, do you see the battalion fire support group of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The command post of the battalion is approximately in the area of Mocina, somewhere between the battalion fire support group and the mortars at the front end, the 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you are familiar with the area of Babin Kuk? Can you indicate it for us, please.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's the area of Babin Kuk. Then the harbour of Gruz, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The area of Lapad? A bit further to south, right.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: These areas that you indicated just now, Babin Kuk, Lapad, the harbour of Gruz, in view of the distance, in terms of the range of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade and the mortar units right behind the front end of the infantry line of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area that we just looked at; Babin Kuk, Lapad, and the harbour of Gruz, the mortars --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you -- could you please focus on the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade. Yes, possibly, possibly. So with 120 and 82-millimetre mortars, the areas that you mentioned can be targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible to target the lower end of the port of Gruz from there, the southernmost part of the harbour of Gruz?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me try to measure it somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Have you got a ruler, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably do. I would like to mention that the measurement is not very precise because this is a photocopied map, and the photocopy was made in a way that would not give the exact distances involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's try.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 120-millimetre mortar of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, then the fire support group, the battalion fire support group, the area that you mentioned, the range, or rather, distance is four to five kilometres. So it is possible to target with these mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Please measure -- thank you. Please measure the distance between the 3rd -- or, rather, the battalion fire support group of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade or, rather, the position in Uskoplje and the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About five and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Five and a half kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, there seems to be a problem with the transcript again. It says, "Please measure the distance between the 3rd -- or, rather, the battalion fire support group of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade or, rather, the position in Uskoplje and the Old Town." Does he want us to measure the one from the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, that fire support group, to the Old Town, or does he want us to measure from Uskoplje to the Old Town again? That's two different concepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague is right. I asked the witness to measure the distance between Uskoplje and the Old Town. That is what we did. Unfortunately, on page 68 in the transcript in lines 18, 19, 20, that cannot be reflected, but that is what I wished to ask the witness, the distance between the battalion fire support group of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd group. That is what I asked.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that right now they did not hear the last sentence of what Mr. Petrovic said. He was not speaking into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It is 5.700 -- 5.770 metres, Mr. Poje, according to our calculations. So that would be roughly what you said as well. Very briefly, we'll move on to this later as well, could you explain to us how come in addendum 1 and addendum 2 that you attached with your report, could you please explain the methodology to us. Were you given certain tasks by the OTP? For example, the position of the mortar, the position of the mortar, say at Zarkovica, the position of the 120-millimetre mortar, or mortar combat position at Zarkovica 120 millimetres or the position of a 120-millimetre mortar at Bosanka or a mortar position, again of a 120-millimetre mortar at Bosanka, how did you get these tasks? How were you given these tasks? Did my colleagues ask you to calculate particular values given a particular position or a particular weapon? Was that the procedure according to which you worked? Is that how you made these calculations? Is that what is in the two addenda?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to look at the dispersion pattern and to calculate it, so then I looked at the previously mentioned battalion, I took the possible positions in the area of Zarkovica, then the area of Bosanka, and as a hypothesis, also the area of Srdj. Then on the basis of the map that we saw yesterday, as for the targets that are around the Old Town, I calculated what the dispersion pattern or ellipse is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, what I do not understand and what I would like you to explain to us is the following: When we know that at the position of Ploce and -- or, rather, the anti-tank position at Zarkovica and at Bosanka and at the position of the 3rd Motorised Company at Strincjera, there are no 120-millimetre mortars, why did you calculate the activities of a 120-millimetre mortar from this position when there weren't any there?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the report that we've already mentioned, too, that is to say concerning the town after the 6th of December, and in this report it says that mortars were shooting at the town, 82-millimetre mortars, and 120-millimetre mortars as well as Maljutkas, quite simply I hypothetically took 82-millimetre mortars and 120-millimetre mortars at these locations. I'm not claiming that they are at those locations. So that's the calculation I did from those locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So quite simply, hypothetically, made this calculation, perhaps if there were mortars there, 82-millimetre or 120-millimetre mortars. On the basis of that hypothesis, you did addendum 1 and addendum 2.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because as we saw on the map, the mortar 82-millimetres are not drawn onto the map, so I just proceeded upon the assumption of what were to happen if 82 mortars were there. We can also see that the 120-millimetre mortars are represented in the back as part of the firing group. So did I that theoretically to look at the dispersion pattern if there was a position at Zarkovica. I was in that area, and you could see that there were positions there at some point. I'm not saying whether they were there on the 6th, but there were some positions. So it was my normal assumption that perhaps there were mortars positioned in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I will show you now an exhibit, a Defence exhibit, and that is -- this is the testimony of Admiral Jokic on page 379 [as interpreted] of the transcript. Admiral Jokic -- 397 [as interpreted]. He describes the position and composition of units around Dubrovnik, and that is primarily the 472nd Brigade. He describes the first unit in the region of Zarkovica and Dubac, saying that it had 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's unclear what they're referring to. It says testimony, which I am assuming trial testimony of Admiral Jokic, and then he says a Defence exhibit, and then he talks about page 379 of a transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As I understand Mr. Petrovic, it's page 372 of the transcript in the course of the evidence of Admiral Jokic and he's going to show the witness a Defence exhibit that was dealt with at that point. Am I nearly right, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, see where the problem is. The problem is that the transcript is not correct. It does not follow what I'm saying. We have the number 379 here. I said 3979. I'm talking about the transcript all the time. I'm speaking of the transcript before this Trial Chamber, so I am quoting what is an exhibit in the sense that it is the transcript before the Trial Chamber and page of that transcript is 3979. I'm not thinking of the interviews, because my learned colleague, of course, knows that an interview cannot be an exhibit in this case. It has not been admitted as an exhibit. So this is not what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we have cleared up the page. I think it would be helpful in future if you referred only to transcript and not regarded it as an exhibit, and that will minimise the scope for any confusion. Thank you. 3979. We've got the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I hope that it is clear now. So 3979.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It states there: "The 1st Company of the -- the 1st Motorised Company, in the Dubac-Zarkovica area, has 82-millimetre mortars. The 2nd Motorised Company, in the Bosanka sector, has 82-millimetre mortars. The 3rd Motorised Company, in Strincjera, has 82-millimetre mortars." Could you please tell me first whether this description corresponds with the formations that are usual when we have motorised companies of a motorised battalion in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is the component of a formation of a motorised company a platoon, an 82-millimetre mortar platoon? Is that a normal part of the motorised company?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it usual that a platoon, an 82-millimetre mortar platoon, is situated directly next to the combat positions of a motorised company?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle it should be somewhat to the rear of the front part of the company disposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So at a slight distance behind.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's not on the front line, but it is a little bit behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So a couple of hundred metres in the back.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So this is the usual formation of a motorised company of a motorised battalion in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When a motorised company of the motorised battalion is used in accordance with the doctrine or the rules of the battalion, the mortar platoon follows in the way that you described the platoons of the motorised company itself?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The doctrine and the manner in which a motorised company is used does not leave room for movements to be made, for separations to be made into one platoon and another platoon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, a unit the strength of a platoon is not usually divided into several parts. It supports the unit as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So we cannot expect an 82-millimetre mortar platoon to be severed from the platoons of the actual motorised platoons of the mechanised -- the motorised company, but they would be concentrated?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Otherwise that would weaken the effectiveness of the support. The greater the concentration of the unit - I'm talking about the mortar unit - the greater the effectiveness is of the support.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So motorised company platoons, infantry platoons, and the mortar platoons would remain, as a rule, in the same zone in accordance with the assignment of the motorised company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On page 3980 of the transcript, Admiral Jokic describes the composition of a battalion fire support group, the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade at Uskoplje, and gives -- and states there that as part of the battalion firing group we have 82-millimetre mortars. My question is as follows: First, what you told us earlier, what is contained in addendum 1 and addendum 2 referring to the use of mortars of 120 millimetres from the sector of Zarkovica, Bosanka and Srdj is, as you have said and I understood, that it is your assumption that perhaps it was like that.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took those points as the most forward points, and I proceeded on the assumption that if 120-millimetre mortars were there, what then would be the effect of the fire from those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So everything that is stated in your report about mortar positions at Zarkovica, Bosanka, and Srdj, 120-millimetre mortar positions, is, let's say, your assumption, and all the conclusions are also a part of that assumption that perhaps 120-millimetre mortars were located there?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If 120-millimetre mortars were not deployed at those positions, you will agree with me that your conclusions from that section of the report are not relevant to our topic that we're discussing here today?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, could you please clarify for us something about the firing tables, the mortar firing tables. So please tell us the table values of dispersion which are given in columns 11 and 12 of the mortar firing tables, and that is, for an example, in Exhibit P172 [as interpreted], those table values in column 11 and 12 are table values of dispersal in ideal conditions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vd and Vp are semi-axes of the dispersion ellipse as a result of accidental errors that occur during firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And now my next question is: What are the table conditions?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The table conditions are --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. I will put the question to you like this: Are the table conditions such that the temperature of the air is 15 degrees?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are the table conditions such that there is no wind?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The table conditions are such that the air pressure is 1.013 MBs?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: One thousand millibars for a 120-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And those table conditions for the 120-millimetre mortar are that the firing targets and the firing position are along one plane?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do the table conditions provide for the firing positions and the target to be at the same altitude?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just very quickly. Sorry to interrupt. At page 75, line 9, it says Exhibit 172. It should be 182. At some future time looking at this we will be confused if we don't correct it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poje, if these values, these table values of dispersal are provided for in the conditions that we have just described, would you agree with me that realistic or realtime dispersal would be different from the values given in the tables?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In true meteorological and ballistic dispersion -- dispersal conditions based on the tables, we calculate the meteorological and the ballistic characteristics and conditions, and we make also topographical corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I think you answered my question but a little -- in a little more detail. The question is: Are the table dispersion values different from realtime, actual dispersal?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The dispersion provided from the -- before the first projectile is fired is theoretical. So the first projectile can fall further or closer from the actual target. When the first projectile actually hits, when we have a first hit, then we are talking about real firing conditions and not on preparation. So by carrying out corrections, we correct errors which occur due to meteorological and ballistic conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you were looking at the potential dispersal that you describe in addendum 1 and addendum 2 to your report, did you actually review the concrete firing conditions in the area that we are talking about in the period of October, November, and December 1991?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about dispersal when the centre hit -- hits the centre of the target. So that means that correction is finished and now we move to group firing. Once again, that means that the calculations that I provided refer to the process once the correction is finished, once the median hit hits the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your realistic assessment of dispersal, did you take into account the conditions prevalent in the area that we are talking about in October, November, and December?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you take into account the conditions as they were on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you take into account the surface conditions, the differences in altitude?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Zarkovica is at an approximate altitude of 300 metres, and the areas around Dubrovnik are at about 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is there a difference in dispersal, keeping in mind the differences in altitude between the firing positions and the target positions?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no difference, only if the target is on a forward or a backward slope, then you would increase or decrease the dispersal. But if the target is above or below the firing position, but if we're talking about a flat surface, then there is no change in the dispersal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How much does the range change if there is a difference in altitude of the firing position and the target?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the firing distance, this would be an average value of 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take the firing tables and look at the graph for the sixth charge of the 120-millimetre mortar, if it's not a problem. Could you please put that on the ELMO. So could we look at the graph for the sixth charge. Could you please move it up a little bit so that we can see the distance up to six kilometres but also so that we can see the beginning, because we need to see the vertical axis on the -- horizontal axis on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: These are ellipses and the parabolas of the trajectory of the mortar projectile; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the parabola at six kilometres which departs from 0.0, from 0 altitude where the range is 6 kilometres, where the range at the same altitude is 6 kilometres. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show -- Mr. Poje, could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what these numbers mean on the left, minus 0.5, 0, 0.5. Is this the altitude?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the altitude taken at half kilometre increments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. So 0 is the altitude that corresponds to the altitude of the target. 0.5 is where the target is below the altitude of the target [as interpreted]. Please, let's not speak at the same time, Mr. Poje. I apologise. So minus 0.5 is 500 metres. So it is when the target is 500 metres in altitude below the firing position from where the mortar projectile was fired?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And now when we are looking at 6 kilometres at the same altitude, so the target is at 0 and the firing position is at 0 altitude also, could you please look at minus 500 metres altitude how much the range is increased, by how much?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: By 230 metres. So at minus 500 altitude, the range is increased by 230 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So how much is the range increased at minus 350 metres? Minus 350 metres.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately by 100 or 120 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So that means that if this is about 250 metres, at minus 350 metres, according to our calculation, it would be somewhat below 200 metres, the increase of range, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think a little less than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But in any case, around 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If -- excuse me for a second. We'll go back to this, Mr. Poje. Let me just move on to some other issues. You told us that in your calculations, you did not take into account meteorological conditions prevailing in October, November, and December, or particularly on the 6th of December. So let me ask you the following: Generally speaking, are you familiar with the weather conditions in the area of Dubrovnik that prevail in these winter months or, rather, late autumn months?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume that it is similar to the conditions in Zadar. There are winter winds and the temperatures are rather low.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in this region of this continental rift there is a clash between the continental and Mediterranean climates?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: According to your experience, do you know of the north-easterly wind called bura, which blows and which is very much present in this region in wintertime?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know about bura, and I know what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is bura by definition a north-easterly wind that blows in general from the land towards the sea?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it blows from the north to the south, to be more precise. It might change directions, and it is possible that it might blow from either north-easterly direction or north-westerly direction, but most definitely from the shore to the sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the shore to the sea. That's the shortest possible definition of bura; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is the impact of a lateral wind on dispersal of shells along the axis?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lateral winds shift the trajectory along the axis either to the left or to the right in respect to the direction of firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that a lateral wind affects the deviation more in case of mortar shells than artillery shells?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because of a very sharp curve of the trajectory, a lateral wind, and also due to the relatively small initial speed of the shell, the wind affects more mortar shell trajectories than other artillery weapon trajectories.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If there is a strong lateral wind, is it sufficient to measure only the wind close to the surface at the firing position?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we do not have meteorological stations that can provide us with meteorological data, then to a certain extent it is a useful information based on which it is possible to calculate meteorological corrections caused by wind, but because of a relatively low height at which wind is being measured and high coordinates, these kind of corrections due to wind is relatively inaccurate. I cannot say exactly in some units, but depending on the wind itself and the instruments used to determine the velocity and the direction of wind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let us try to simplify this. If we are measuring only the wind close to the surface at the -- during firing, only during firing a mortar shell, the error may be quite substantial.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is possible. We even did some calculations, and we concluded that in certain cases it is even better not to take into account corrections valid at the level close to the surface but just to take them into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there is a difference between the wind close to the ground and the winds at higher altitudes?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. There are examples when wind close to the earth can blow in a different direction than the one blowing at an altitude of two kilometres. The only way to establish that is by using balloons or meteorological stations that can easily measure these by using a probe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about whether in this region that we're discussing now there were conditions in place to measure winds at higher altitudes by using meteorological probes during the fire opened from mortars?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly speaking, I don't know if there was one nearby, whether there was any meteorological station nearby preparing daily reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there could have been substantial error because it was impossible to measure wind at higher altitudes?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible, but initial elements can be determined with a high margin of error. However, this error is corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your experience, is bura a constant wind or is it characterised by strong gusts of wind?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bura is not a constantly blowing wind. It comes in gusts. It could stop altogether and then suddenly start blowing again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do infantry units, company- or battalion-strong infantry units, have at all any meteorological balloons, probes, or other instruments?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Infantry battalion, which means mortar units within it, has no possibility to set up a meteorological station. They don't have such units that do meteorological reconnaissance for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your report, did you include any data about the strength of the wind and the impact or the influence of the wind on dispersal of shells on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if we look at this map which I hope is still before you, Exhibit P132, can you please be so kind as to tell the Honourable Chamber - and I don't think it will be difficult for you to do so by looking at the map - to tell us the altitude above sea level of motorised companies of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade. Can you just give us an estimate for Strincjera, for example?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the altitude above sea level is between 300 and 400 metres in the area between Srdj and Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That would mean that Strincjera is at about 412 metres.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, although it is relatively difficult to determine this precisely on such a small-scale map. We know that at 300 metres is Zarkovica, that Srdj is at 500 metres, although Bosanka is a little bit lower at some 250 metres, then it rises again towards Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, that means that these positions, if there had been any positions at all of mortars in that area -- region, were at the altitudes between 300 or 400 or a little bit over 400 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 300 and 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the position of the battalion fire group at Uskoplje and tell us, please, your estimate of the altitude above sea level where this firing group was.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can see well, it's 597 metres, and the battery and firing group is a little bit lower, I think at about 500 metres. This is just an approximation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave and your approval, I would suggest that we adjourn for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
